source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent updates vendor bank details whenever an invoice shows new bank details, with no independent verification of the requester or the new account, and no distinction between a routine invoice detail and a security-sensitive payment-routing change.

The only stated safeguard before an irreversible payment or bank-detail change is asking a clerk to approve a one-line model-generated summary. The safeguard's content (what the clerk sees) is entirely determined by the model, with no structural requirement to surface the underlying bank account or change history.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate itself runs outside the model, but the approver sees only the model's one-line summary, not the destination bank account or change history (approval_review_mode: model_summary). A more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary defeats it (ASI09), and it fails further under model_upgrade and autonomy_increase. High daily volume (~150 cards/day) compounds this through approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: An independent, out-of-band check (e.g., a callback to a phone number already on file, not one supplied by the invoice) does not depend on model behavior and is not currently present.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review showing destination account and diff
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the clerk the actual bank account number, an old-versus-new diff, and change history (rather than a model summary) removes the model's ability to shape what the approver sees.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoping
controls.decay_rationale: Currently the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (credential_scope: broad on both capabilities). Scoping it per-vendor or per-transaction would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Spend cap and bank-change-then-payment anomaly detection
controls.decay_rationale: A hold or alert when a bank-detail change is immediately followed by a payment to the same vendor, plus monitoring of per-clerk approval volume, would be detective/containment and does not currently exist.

findings.title: TC9: Summary-gated approval on an invoice-driven bank change and irreversible payment

attack_path.note: Untrusted supplier-submitted invoice claims new bank details for an existing vendor.
Agent reads the existing vendor master record to match the invoice to a vendor and PO.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details based on invoice content, with no independent verification.
Clerk sees only a one-line model-generated summary; bank account number and change history are withheld.
Agent schedules an irreversible payment to the vendor's (possibly now fraudulent) bank account, gated by the same summary card.

forecast.watch_signal: The model backing this agent is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true); or clerk approval volume (currently ~150 cards/day) keeps rising toward levels associated with rubber-stamping (SAFE-T1403). Either signal means the summary-gated approval control can no longer be relied on to catch a fabricated bank-detail change.

evidence.observation: Agent updates vendor bank details whenever an invoice shows new bank details, with no independent verification step described.
The only stated safeguard before any payment or bank change is a human approval request built from a one-line model-generated summary.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The card shows vendor name, amount, invoice id, and PO match, but not the destination bank account number or whether/how bank details recently changed.

Bank account numbers and change history are not shown to the clerk; the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Change the approval gate to raw_action review: show the clerk the actual destination bank account, a diff against the prior bank details, and the change history before allowing a payment or bank change to proceed. Do not rely on a model-generated summary for this decision.

Require change-managed review whenever the underlying model is upgraded (set subject.model.swappable to false, or trigger a mandatory reassessment on upgrade), since the approval gate's effectiveness is partially dependent on the model's summary text.

Add independent out-of-band verification of any vendor bank-detail change (e.g., a callback to a phone number already on file, never one supplied by the invoice) before the change takes effect, decoupled from the invoice-processing agent.
Scope the ERP credential used by the agent to least privilege (e.g., restrict which vendors and payment amounts it can act on) instead of granting update-any-vendor and schedule-any-payment access.

Add anomaly detection that holds or flags any payment scheduled shortly after a bank-detail change to the same vendor, and monitor per-clerk approval volume and approval latency for fatigue thresholds.

rating.rationale: An untrusted supplier invoice (U) can drive an irreversible outbound payment (S3: action=spend, is_egress=true, reversibility=irreversible), and can first rewrite the vendor's bank details (S3-relevant: restricted data, irreversible in effect once payment follows) with no independent verification. Inherent risk is critical (U x S3). The only declared control is a human approval gate on both sensitive capabilities, which is structural and earns the rubric's -2 tier credit, but because the clerk sees only a model-generated one-line summary (approval_review_mode: model_summary) rather than the raw destination account and change history, the residual floor of 'moderate' applies rather than a lower tier. No other structural containment (credential scoping, out-of-band verification, spend caps) is declared. Because the approval gate's effectiveness is partially dependent on the model's summary quality, an explicitly stated trigger -- the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review -- defeats this control (ASI09, SAFE-T1403), and the forecast reverts to the critical inherent level. High approval volume (~150/day) is recorded as a compounding watch signal for approval fatigue rather than a separate schema trigger.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md, the approval card artifact, and the runtime notes. It does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.
No MCP configuration, IaC, or source code was provided; capability and credential scope are taken as declared in the runtime notes rather than independently verified.
No logging or audit trail artifact was provided, so no detective control beyond the stated approval card could be credited.

Workflow engine details (whether schedule_payment is technically blocked pending approval, or the approval step is only a prompted behavior) were not fully specified; the approval gate was scored as structural per the runtime notes' description of a shown approval card, but this should be verified against the actual orchestration implementation.
